analysis:
All three changed files are test-only. Each change updates a stub LanguageModel conformance in a private test class: `prepare(_:cache:windowSize:)` becomes `prepare(_:cache:state:prefill:)`. The change sits at ProviderMTPFactoryTests.swift:28, SpecDecCapacityTests.swift:273 and ReserveRaisePreflightTests.swift:254. It tracks a new mlx-swift-lm protocol signature. The stubs return `.tokens(input.text)` and have empty caches, so they hold no keys, prompts, attestation material, network I/O or serving authorization.

I saw no production source, so the Package.swift or dependency pin that introduces the new `LanguageModel` protocol shape is not in the supplied evidence. That upstream dependency change is a supply-chain and API-semantics question for TB-007, outside this batch. The base `windowSize` parameter is replaced by `state` and `prefill`. Any real model's change in prefill windowing or state handling, which affects T-041 prefix-cache and KV behavior and T-028 residual data, would live in production code that I could not review.

The ProviderMTPFactoryTests head text also exercises the cached catalog assistant revalidation path: SHA-256 manifest and file verification, corruption fallback to `warmArtifactCorrupt`, and local override mutation falling back to `localArtifactInvalid` before the loader runs. These tests are not modified beyond the stub signature. No weakened assertion or new attack surface was identified.

No findings. Remaining integration question: confirm the production LanguageModel conformances and the dependency bump handle the new `state` and `prefill` parameters without altering cache scoping, TTL, salt handling or memory-grant behavior.
